newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Brent seen down if "rounding bottom" sags.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Brent seen down if "rounding bottom" sags.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* A "rounding bottom" style pattern made up from last week's lows of the five trading days suggests the chances of some upside action are increased in the short term, chartists said.
* But analysts expect prices to dip in the next couple of days after attempts to break to the upside failed on Friday.

IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures may see a small short-covering led up-tick in early trade, but analysts expect prices to dip in the next couple of days after attempts to break to the upside failed on Friday.

Brokers said technical and speculative fund buying on Friday failed to break through key resistance around $17.90 a barrel leaving bearish sentiment intact. They expected that after initial support from short-covering in early trade prices could start to dip back again.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International, Gainesville, Georgia said in his daily report that he saw no meaningful changes in the markets outlook brought by the roll to August.
However, he expected prices will fall to under $17.61 this week, although from a subjective point of view.

"I'd rather see this next fall begin over the next couple of days or so from above $18.12-15, but even if the price falls under $17.61 today with Friday's high intact that is not a big bottom and we still have at least several more days of a wide range trading environment to deal with before the fall from $20.60 on May 16 ends."

Peter Sceats refers to the peek and trough tenet of Dow theory in his weekly report. "This says that the interruption of a series of peaks and troughs is often a pre-cursor to a change in trend," Sceats explained.
He said "on this basis the there can be no question that the move below $17.54 on the spot month continuation and weekly charts has considerably worsened the technical profile of the Brent market."
"This trough failure added to the peak failure that occurred when prices did not top $20.84 in the previous rally could be seen to set the market up for a down move, later if not sooner," he added.

However, he said that a "rounding bottom" style pattern made up from last week's lows of the five trading days suggests the chances of some upside action are increased in the short term if the market can prevail above the base of the rounding bottom.
That base is $17.32 on the spot month continuation chart and $17.61 on the August chart.
"But if a print below here occurs the pattern is negated and it's back to further downside action," Sceats warns.

Graham took a neutral stance on gas oil but advised near term caution with no major bottom in place yet. He said recent gains were mainly corrective and the market may even push up to $164 in the next day or so, but this will be followed by a drop under $161.25.
"The price will probably fall under $159.50 and later towards $150 after a bounce," Graham said. He said resistance lies at $170 if $164.50 is exceeded with $161.25 support left intact.

August Brent was quoted on SIMEX at $17.80/$18.00 per barrel, up from the London close of $17.76. On ACCESS NYMEX August crude oil was last traded at $19.12 per barrel, up six cents from the close on Friday. July was last traded at $18.90, up seven cents.
July gas oil ended 25 cents up at $162.75 a tonne off from a high of $164.50.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
